But two days after being exposed to police teargas during France’s nationwide protests on 17 October, she began bleeding heavily.

French police fired about 22,000 teargas grenades at protesters on 17 October at the height of the protests – equivalent to two grenades every three seconds (over 10 hours of maintaining order).

items.title: [politico.eu] EU budget talks collapse after seven net contributors skip sessions
items.content_html: Seven net-contributor governments refused to attend some of European Council President António Costa’s small-group budget meetings in Brussels, disputing both the proposed cuts to the European Union’s 2028-2034 spending plan and the negotiating process. The summit ended without agreement, and leaders cancelled its planned second day. The budget covers EU farm and regional-development funds, with some governments pressing to shift spending toward defence and competitiveness. The talks centred on Costa’s proposed €1.78 trillion framework, already about €204 billion below the European Commission’s original plan. German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said the package needed deeper reductions, while French President Emmanuel Macron called the cuts a strategic error and opposed further reductions. Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni warned that Italy would not accept paying more while receiving less. EU leaders are due back in Brussels on Dec. 17-18 and still aim to reach a deal by year-end. The proposed €45 billion loan for Ukraine also remained contested: Costa said 24 of the 27 member states supported it, while Bulgaria sought to limit its contribution to non-military assistance.

items.title: [france24.com] Trump urges Putin to halt European aggression as Ukraine war intensifies
items.content_html: President Donald Trump said on Nov. 26 that he had urged Russian President Vladimir Putin during talks in China the previous week to pull back “all military aggression” across Europe. He said he hoped that could lead to a quick deal to end the war in Ukraine but did not specify which territories or actions he meant. His statement followed a Florida meeting with NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte, after which they called on Russia and Ukraine to avoid steps that could widen the war. At their China meeting, Trump greeted Putin as a “friend,” worrying officials in Kyiv and European capitals. Russian strikes hit Kyiv overnight, wounding seven people, while Ukraine’s president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, warned of another possible mass attack. European concern has also grown after missiles landed in Poland. Washington has delayed a review of the U.S. military presence in Europe beyond its provisional Dec. 1 deadline while it assesses options and European offers to replace some U.S. capabilities. The review will go to Trump, but officials have not set a date for a decision.

items.title: [abcnews.com] Guinea-Bissau junta delays presidential and parliamentary elections until 2028
items.content_html: Guinea-Bissau’s military government has postponed presidential and parliamentary elections until Nov. 26, 2028, extending its promised one-year transition to civilian rule by about two years. Transitional President Gen. Horta N’Tam set the date in a Nov. 26 decree on the anniversary of the 2025 coup. The elections had been scheduled for Dec. 6, 2026. The junta said technical, material and financial preparations were inadequate to ensure a credible vote. The army seized power three days after the November 2025 general election, before officials announced the results. Incumbent President Umaro Sissoco Embaló and opposition candidate Fernando Dias both claimed victory. In August 2026, voters approved a military-organized constitutional referendum that strengthened presidential powers and reduced the size of parliament; the opposition had called for a boycott. N’Tam said the transition required more time and resources for electoral reforms, including a nationwide voter census and new constituency boundaries. The junta also says it needs to hold the country’s first municipal elections in 2027. The regional bloc ECOWAS has urged a short, structured and transparent return to civilian rule.

items.title: [ft.com] Italy and Germany warn Ukraine against widening war after Libya strikes
items.content_html: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni and German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul warned Ukraine against widening its war with Russia after Ukrainian drones struck Russian vessels in and off Benghazi, Libya, on Nov. 22. Kyiv said the operation targeted Russian military assets; Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky confirmed responsibility the following day. Ukraine said the corvette Merkury sank and a cargo ship used to carry military equipment was hit. Meloni said Italy would continue helping Ukraine defend itself but must also protect its own citizens and borders. Wadephul also affirmed Ukraine’s right to self-defense while warning against escalation and risks to Baltic shipping and the environment. Rome’s concerns include Libya’s proximity, energy links and role in migration routes. Italy also said it had not been told about the operation in advance. Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha told his Libyan counterpart that Kyiv did not intend to extend the war to Libya or any other country. Libya’s internationally recognized government condemned the operation, while Italy is considering additional security measures for about 200 Italian troops there. Wadephul said Germany was in close talks on containing escalation and protecting maritime traffic.

The provincial River Forecast Centre issued a flood warning for central Island waterways, where rivers had reached their banks or were expected to overflow soon. Officials said eastern Vancouver Island remained under a flood watch and coastal flood warnings continued in many areas. Courtenay declared a local emergency and ordered evacuations from several low-lying properties, including the Maple Pool campground, while the Regional District of Nanaimo ordered some Cedar residents to leave homes along the Nanaimo River. Rain and wind warnings for the South Coast were lifted Thursday, but officials said rivers would need time to recede before advisories could be withdrawn. The Effingham Island weather station recorded 469 millimetres of rain in just over two days.

items.title: [euronews.com] EU leaders confront deeper cuts as farmers, regions defend funding
items.content_html: European Union leaders began two days of budget talks in Brussels on Thursday, with national governments disputing how much to spend and whether to shift money from farm subsidies and poorer regions to defence and competitiveness. European Council President António Costa’s revised 2028-2034 plan cuts €204 billion from the European Commission’s original proposal, bringing the proposed budget to about €1.582 trillion; roughly €740 billion would support farmers and poorer regions. The negotiations also cover a proposed €45 billion Ukraine loan, which German Chancellor Friedrich Merz wants all 27 member states to support as a condition for a wider budget deal. Net contributors including Germany want a smaller overall package, while the 17-member Friends of Cohesion group opposes further cuts to regional funding. France is pressing to preserve farm income support, while Greece has said it will not accept further cuts to cohesion and Common Agricultural Policy funding. Costa’s proposal would raise new EU revenue, including through a digital tax, but new revenue sources require unanimous approval. Leaders are expected to use the Brussels meeting to clarify positions rather than settle the budget. A final deal requires unanimity, and a further summit is scheduled for Dec. 17-18; France has warned that negotiations should not run beyond December, ahead of elections in 2027.

items.title: [finchannel.com] Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant switches to diesel after grid line cut
items.content_html: A Russian attack knocked out the 330-kilovolt Ferrosplavna-1 line at 4:28 a.m. on Nov. 25, cutting external power to the Russian-occupied Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant and leaving its essential systems reliant on backup diesel generators, Ukraine’s state nuclear operator Energoatom said. The line was cut after an attack on the right bank of the Dnipro River, about 13 kilometers from the Ferrosplavna substation. The International Atomic Energy Agency said it was the plant’s 28th loss of all external power since Russia’s full-scale invasion began; Ukraine’s energy ministry counted it as the 17th such outage this year. IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi said agency experts at the plant were investigating where and why the line disconnected. Energoatom warned that repeated damage near the facility increases the risk of a nuclear accident.

Seoul also urged Pyongyang to stop justifying its nuclear development and comply with U.N. Security Council resolutions. Kim made the remarks during a Nov. 25 tour of nuclear-material and weapons-research facilities, including a nuclear-powered equipment production base whose location state media did not disclose. He said North Korea was systematically expanding nuclear-material output and should use tactical weapons for different missions across multiple domains, citing the border with South Korea. Analysts cited by The Straits Times said the equipment base may be producing submarine reactors and parts, potentially for a nuclear-powered submarine planned for 2027. South Korean experts said Kim’s position appeared aimed at making future U.S.-North Korea talks focus on arms control between nuclear-armed states rather than denuclearization.

items.title: [allafrica.com] Somalia orders UAE ambassador out within 72 hours in diplomatic rift
items.content_html: Somalia’s government on Nov. 19 ordered the United Arab Emirates ambassador to leave within 72 hours and recalled its own envoy from Abu Dhabi after President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud accused the UAE of interfering in Somali affairs, backing armed groups and making port deals with regional administrations without federal approval. The UAE rejected Mogadishu’s accusations, calling its approach “escalatory and hostile,” and said it had already closed its embassy and withdrawn its diplomats in January after Somalia canceled bilateral agreements. The dispute involves UAE relations with Somaliland, Puntland and Jubaland, as well as disagreements within Somalia over constitutional changes and election arrangements. Parliament amended the constitution in March to extend presidential and parliamentary terms from four years to five; regional administrations and opposition figures rejected the changes. Somalia’s Supreme Court later ruled that the current leaders’ terms had expired and set deadlines for an election framework and polls.

items.title: [eldia.com.do] Car bomb in Villavicencio leaves more than 20 injured on anniversary of peace deal
items.content_html: On November 24, Colombia commemorated the tenth anniversary of the peace deal signed in Bogotá between the government and the FARC guerrillas. The day before, a car bomb exploded in Villavicencio, leaving more than 20 people injured. President Abelardo de la Espriella blamed the attack on FARC dissidents and ruled out negotiating with armed groups. The agreement ended more than half a century of conflict between the government and the guerrillas; more than 13,600 combatants laid down their arms. A decade later, the Kroc Institute estimates that 36% of the commitments have been fulfilled. The Office of the Ombudsman records 521 signatories killed, and the Armed Forces estimate that armed groups total around 29,000 members across 165 structures, compared with approximately 13,000 in 2022. After the FARC withdrew, the government failed to establish a sufficient presence in several areas, which were left vulnerable to disputes among other groups. De la Espriella has cut the budget of the Special Jurisdiction for Peace (JEP), the court created by the agreement, and ended talks with armed groups. Former president Juan Manuel Santos maintains that the problems stem from the failure to implement the agreement. At the request of the Colombian government and with the backing of the United States, the UN verification mission will stop monitoring rural reform; its overall mandate was renewed for one year.

items.content_html: China and India are on track for record seaborne Russian oil imports averaging 3.4 million barrels per day in 2026, based on figures through mid-November, about 530,000 barrels per day more than a year earlier. The Iran war disrupted Middle Eastern supplies, while temporary U.S. sanctions waivers eased purchases and Ukrainian drone attacks reduced Russian refining capacity, leaving more crude available for export. Traders and analysts expect purchases to ease in 2027 if Middle Eastern supply recovers. China’s Russian oil imports averaged 2.34 million barrels per day in January-October, while India’s averaged 1.87 million barrels per day over the same period.

items.title: [thenationalnews.com] Black Sea attacks threaten grain routes as shipping costs rise
items.content_html: The United Nations warned that drone attacks on commercial vessels are threatening food exports as the Russia-Ukraine war spreads across shipping lanes. From June through October, the U.N. human rights office recorded reports of 164 attacks on commercial vessels around Ukraine’s Odesa and Mykolaiv regions and in the Black Sea; it verified 15 attacks that killed at least 21 vessel workers and injured 43. Recent strikes have also reached the Baltic and waters off Libya, while a maritime risk zone was extended on Nov. 18 toward Romania and Bulgaria. The disruption is raising freight and insurance costs and shifting grain purchases toward European suppliers, but prices are moving unevenly: Euronext’s December wheat contract closed Nov. 23 at €240.25 a tonne, up €3.50, while Constanța bread-wheat and corn quotes fell 1.7% and 1.3%. More Argentine and Australian wheat could become available to buyers in coming weeks.

items.title: [cbc.ca] Quebec court suspends province’s exemption from Crown oath
items.content_html: Quebec Superior Court Justice Ian Demers suspended the province’s 2022 exemption from the Crown oath required of lawmakers across Canada, saying Quebec could not change the constitutional requirement on its own. Premier Paul St-Pierre Plamondon says he will appeal. The dispute could affect the legal standing of legislation passed by Quebec’s newly elected assembly, while the underlying challenge has yet to be heard on its merits. Ottawa lawyer Lawrence David, who brought the case, says the oath requirement applies to the King as Canada’s head of state. Laval University constitutional law professor Patrick Taillon argues that courts could temporarily preserve laws later found invalid, citing a Supreme Court remedy in a Manitoba language case. Quebec’s legislature is scheduled to resume Dec. 1.
